items.title: Where you measure changes what the doubling ratio tells you
items.description: For T(n) = 3n² + 100n, the doubling ratio T(2n)/T(n) isn't constant — it depends on where you measure it. Drag the slider to move the measurement point n from small (linear-looking) to large (unmistakably quadratic), and watch the ratio climb toward its true asymptotic value of 4.
items.compute: const t1 = 3 * params.measurementN * params.measurementN + 100 * params.measurementN; const n2 = params.measurementN * 2; const t2 = 3 * n2 * n2 + 100 * n2; const doublingRatio = Math.round((t2 / t1) * 100) / 100; return { doublingRatio };
